batchName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Empire: Roman Art and Architecture (c. 500 BC-AD 476)

questions.question: Which emperor rebuilt the Pantheon in its present form?
questions.explanation: Hadrian was a passionate builder. His Pantheon, a temple to all the gods, is the best-preserved temple of the ancient world.
questions.sourceQuote: Hadrian rebuilt the Pantheon, a temple to all the gods, in its present form.

questions.question: Where in an aristocratic Roman house were ancestral busts put on display?
questions.explanation: Busts of ancestors stood in the atrium, the entrance hall that visitors saw first. At funerals, masks of forebears were even worn in procession.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancestral busts were displayed in the entrance hall (*atrium*) of an aristocratic house, and at the funerals of great families, masks of the forebears (*imagines*) were worn in procession.

questions.question: Which art form was the Romans' one great artistic strength of their own?
questions.explanation: The Roman portrait grew out of a deep reverence for family. Ancestral busts were proudly displayed in aristocratic homes.
questions.sourceQuote: If the Romans had one great artistic strength of their own, it was the portrait.

questions.question: Where did most Roman city dwellers live?
questions.explanation: Insulae could rise up to five storeys. They were cramped, unhealthy and prone to fire.
questions.sourceQuote: Most city dwellers lived not in houses but in apartment blocks (*insulae*), up to five storeys high.

questions.question: Which famous Roman aqueduct bridge still stands in southern France?
questions.explanation: The Pont du Gard survives in southern France. The aqueduct of Segovia also still stands, but in Spain.
questions.sourceQuote: The Pont du Gard in southern France and the aqueduct of Segovia in Spain still stand.

questions.question: Constantine moved the capital to Constantinople. What was that city once called?
questions.explanation: The city on the Bosporus had been Byzantium. There Roman art absorbed eastern influences and grew into the Byzantine style.
questions.sourceQuote: When Constantine moved the capital to Constantinople, the city on the Bosporus once called Byzantium, Roman art absorbed eastern influences and grew into the Byzantine style.

questions.question: Which material is credited with a 'revolution' in Roman architecture?
questions.explanation: Concrete existed earlier in the Near East, but the Romans perfected it and made it the backbone of their grandest buildings. It was cheap and easy to transport.
questions.sourceQuote: Historians call the result the "concrete revolution".

questions.question: What did Augustus famously boast about the city of Rome?
options: He found it small and left it the largest city
He found it in ruins and rebuilt it in a decade
He found it wooden and left it bronze
He found it brick and left it marble
questions.explanation: It was an exaggeration, since marble was mostly a facing over brick or concrete. Still, his reign opened the Carrara quarries for the capital.
questions.sourceQuote: Augustus, Rome's first emperor (27 BC–AD 14), famously boasted that he had found Rome a city of brick and left it a city of marble.

questions.question: The sack of which wealthy Greek city in 146 BC sent many Greek artists to Rome as slaves?
questions.explanation: After Corinth fell in 146 BC, many of its artists were carried off as slaves. By the 2nd century BC most sculptors working in Rome were Greek.
questions.sourceQuote: After the sack of Corinth, a wealthy Greek city, in 146 BC, many Greek artists were carried off as slaves.

questions.question: Trajan's Column tells the story of his wars in which region, now modern Romania?
questions.explanation: The campaigns unfold in a carved band spiralling about 200 m around the shaft. The column was dedicated in AD 113.
questions.sourceQuote: Trajan's Column, dedicated in AD 113, tells the story of his wars in Dacia, modern Romania, in a carved band spiralling about 200 m (650 feet) around the shaft.
